summary.text: André Carson is the Democratic incumbent for Indiana's 7th Congressional District (Indianapolis). An Indianapolis native who worked in law enforcement and state counterterrorism work and served briefly on the City-County Council, he won a March 2008 special election to succeed his late grandmother, Rep. Julia Carson. He is a member of the House Intelligence Committee and a Senior Whip for House Democrats.

paragraphs.text: Carson was born in Indianapolis in 1974, raised on the city's east side, and graduated from Arsenal Technical High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice management from Concordia University-Wisconsin and a master's degree in business management from Indiana Wesleyan University.

Before entering office he worked in law enforcement, including as a compliance officer with the Indiana State Excise Police from 1996 to 2005. He later worked in the anti-terrorism division of the Indiana Department of Homeland Security, including at the Indiana Intelligence Fusion Center.

Carson was a Democratic precinct committeeperson in Indianapolis. In 2007 a Marion County Democratic caucus chose him to fill a seat on the Indianapolis City-County Council, where he served until 2008.

He won a March 11, 2008 special election to the 7th District seat after the death of his grandmother, Rep. Julia Carson, who had held it since 1997, and was sworn in on March 13, 2008. He was the second Muslim ever elected to the U.S. Congress.

In the 2025-2026 Congress Carson serves on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (National Intelligence Enterprise; National Security Agency and Cyber subcommittees), the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials subcommittees), and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

According to his House biography, he chaired the Intelligence Committee's Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation Subcommittee, which held the first congressional hearing on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in more than 50 years, and he serves as a Senior Whip for the House Democratic Caucus. He is a former member of the House Financial Services Committee.
The same biography lists his caucus memberships as including the Congressional Black Caucus, the Progressive Caucus, the New Democrat Coalition, and the LGBT Equality Caucus.
